highlighted: As someone who lives in Portugal which already stops every single package you get from outside EU with no exceptions for a decade or more
oldNote: Exceptions exist: gifts under €45 between individuals are VAT/duty-exempt, and IOSS pre-cleared shipments pass through without extra VAT collection. Also, the universal customs clearance rule for all packages only began EU-wide on 1 July 2021, not a decade or more ago.
newNote: Not every non-EU package is stopped: gifts up to €45 and low-value goods (≤€150) are often exempt from duty, and checks are risk-based, not universal. The strict VAT/customs handling stems from EU-wide rules effective July 2021, not a decade-old Portuguese policy.

highlighted: Fact checker Megan Herbst gets the facts wrong in Wired, claims AI fact checking cannot be trusted based exclusively on AI overviews.
oldNote: Herbst's WIRED piece did not rely on Google's "AI Overviews." She cited a Tow Center/CJR study of 8 AI search tools (60%+ citation error rate) and a BBC/EBU study of chatbots (~45% error rate), plus fact-checkers like Full Fact. Her name is Meghan, not Megan.
newNote: Herbst's WIRED piece grounds its argument mainly in WIRED's own line-by-line fact-checking process, her personal chatbot tests, and how AI models are trained on internet text versus offline archives—not exclusively on Google's AI Overviews product.
